summary: The ShruggieTech inheritance root. Every sub-brand kit is generated against this file. Values marked immutable are copied verbatim and never re-decided. Values marked constrained are chosen per sub-brand but must satisfy the stated rule, which is machine-checkable. Everything else is free.

provenance.contrast_method: WCAG 2.1 relative luminance, re-derived from hex by coloraide at generation time
provenance.rule: No contrast number in this file was typed by hand. Regenerate rather than edit.

confidence_labels.VERIFIED BY INSPECTION: checked against real installed files or measured from real values
confidence_labels.RESEARCH-SOURCED: from provider documentation, not independently confirmed here

tiers.immutable: Inherited verbatim. A sub-brand that changes one of these is not a ShruggieTech sub-brand.
tiers.constrained: Chosen per sub-brand, must satisfy the attached machine-checkable rule.

hard_rules: Never introduce a fourth family. Domain needs are met with the three above.
Geist ships 400 and 500 only. Geist Mono ships 400 only. Requesting a weight that does not exist makes the renderer synthesise a faux bold, which prints badly and forces outlined glyphs into PDFs.
In mono contexts carry emphasis with color, never with weight.
Sentence case is the default. Uppercase is reserved for compact labels and table metadata.
Disable ligatures and smart-quote substitution on code, pre, kbd and samp.

sourcing.evidence: VERIFIED BY INSPECTION of installed skills, 2026-08-22. Not inferred.
sourcing.rule: Bundle the binaries. Do not fetch fonts at build time.

order.source: Bundled in the kit at assets/fonts/
order.why: No network, nothing to fail. This is what shruggie-docs already does (six TTFs, 703KB, embedded into every emitted .docx) and what Anthropic's own `morning` skill does (fraunces woff2, base64'd into a data URI).
order.applies_to: anything the skill itself renders: PDFs, DOCX, specimens, static HTML mocks, social previews

order.source: npm packages in the GENERATED project
order.why: Different context from rank 1. A Next.js project the kit scaffolds uses `geist` (geist/font/sans, geist/font/mono) and next/font/google for Space Grotesk. The build machine has registry access; the skill sandbox may not.
order.applies_to: the consumer application, never the skill's own rendering path

order.why: Document where the bundled bytes came from so they can be refreshed. Never a runtime or build-time request.
order.applies_to: the refresh procedure, documented in the kit README

sourcing.hard_warning: fonts.gstatic.com is BLOCKED by the egress proxy in the Claude sandbox. fonts.googleapis.com (the CSS) resolves, so a Google Fonts fetch appears to succeed and then fails at the binary step with a 403 tunnel error or curl exit 56. Any build path that reaches for Google Fonts is broken by construction.
sourcing.flat_knowledge_caveat: In a FLAT KNOWLEDGE upload (Gemini Gems knowledge, Custom GPT Knowledge) a font binary is inert, because those surfaces have no filesystem and no execution. That is a statement about what can be USED there, and it is not an argument against bundling. The skill-package path is unaffected.
sourcing.size_budget: Six TTFs run about 700KB. Claude's Skills API allows 30MB total and OpenAI allows 50MB. Fonts are not near any limit.

scripting.note: PowerShell in skill packages is fine and already in use: shruggie-powershell ships six .ps1 files, shruggie-markdown and shruggie-speckit ship one each. The only real constraint is the execution host.
scripting.rule: Write build and verify scripts that must run inside the Claude or OpenAI cloud sandbox in Python, because those containers are Linux. PowerShell is correct for anything targeting a Windows workstation via Claude Code, which is the ShruggieTech house environment.

density.rule: Every kit ships BOTH. A product switches per screen. A sub-brand does not pick one as its baseline.

compact.use_when: dense tabular data: packet rows, schedule grids, log views

color.tier_note: The identity accent is constrained. Everything else here is immutable.

orange.note: The lineage thread. Every sub-brand inherits this exact value even when it shares no other color with the parent. fragcap kept it while sharing zero else.

orange-cta.note: Legal as a FILL with white text. Illegal as text on the dark base (measured below).

fault.note: Promoted to canon from fragcap 1.1.0. The parent canon had no failure color at all.

gray-600.role: muted text on LIGHT surfaces only

gray-400.role: muted text on DARK surfaces only

parent_identity_accent.note: ShruggieTech's own accent. A sub-brand replaces this trio with its own, subject to the rule below.

accessible.note: NEW in canon 1.0.0. Derived at hue 152.99 to clear 5:1 on the light base. The parent kit set bright green as the light-mode link color, which measures 1.98:1 and is a live accessibility defect.

dark_surfaces.rule: One hue family, OKLCH lightness between 0.10 and 0.22, chroma at or below 0.030. Subtle depth as the page scrolls, never obvious.

checks.rule: OKLCH hue at least 30 degrees from every existing sibling IDENTITY accent.
checks.scope_note: Compare identity accents only. go-schedule's Interval Mint sits 18.8 degrees from green but is a semantic success color, not the identity accent, so it is out of scope for this check.

checks.rule: At least 4.5:1 against the dark base.
A separate accessible variant clearing 4.5:1 against the light base MUST exist. The bright accent is almost never legal as text on light.
The legal text color on top of the accent fill must be measured and recorded, never assumed.
At least 30 degrees from the inherited orange at hue 38.3, so emphasis stays distinguishable from identity.

chart_palette.rule: Derived from the identity accent by formula, never hand-picked. Rotate hue by 0, -52, +52, -104, +104 degrees off the accent; hold chroma at 0.92x for entries 2-5; then SOLVE lightness against the actual surface, taking the value closest to the target that still clears 4.5:1.

target_lightness.on_dark: the accent's own OKLCH lightness, clamped to 0.58-0.82
target_lightness.on_light: the ACCESSIBLE variant's own lightness, clamped to 0.35-0.62

two_failure_modes_this_guards_against: A palette tuned for a black background is too pale to read on near-white. Solve against the real surface.
A naive solve runs entries to near-monochrome extremes that technically pass at 9:1 and lose the brand. Take the value closest to target, not the first one found.
Do not re-darken on the light path. The accessible variant is already darkened; darkening twice produces the 9:1 failure above.

icons.why_immutable: Icon set is the single biggest source of agent drift and standardising costs nothing. Two ShruggieTech products must not read as two companies.
icons.rendering: inline SVG so icons inherit the semantic text token of their container
icons.bespoke_icons: A sub-brand MAY draw domain icons that lucide lacks (a packet lane, a cron cell). They are drawn to the same 24 grid and stroke spec and shipped in the kit's icons/ directory. Swapping to a different icon library is not permitted.
icons.third_party_logos: Use the entity-icon PNGs from the ShruggieTech CDN index rather than redrawing another company's mark.

motion.rule: Interface transitions between 120ms and 300ms on an approved easing. Decorative loops are permitted only if they respect prefers-reduced-motion.

rules: Every interactive element carries a visible 2px focus ring at 2px offset, driven by :focus-visible.
Status is never carried by color alone. Every state ships a label or a shape.
Respect prefers-reduced-motion on every transition and animation.
The bright identity accent is never body text on a light surface. Use the accessible variant.
Contrast claims are re-derived from hex on every build. A kit that ships a transcribed ratio fails verify.

endorsement.placement: footer, About page, repository metadata, title-page colophon, social preview
rules: Visually subordinate to the product's own mark.
Outside the product logo's clear space.
Never combine the parent mark and the product mark into a single lockup.

registers.direct-witty: parent ShruggieTech: confidently scrappy, we/you, sparing humour
registers.precise-dry: fragcap: technically literate, states prerequisites and limits

shruggie_flourish.rule: Opt-in per sub-brand. At most one moment per view, always in the identity accent. fragcap correctly declines it: a security-adjacent tool should not wink.

banned_rhetoric.why: The most recognisable tell of machine-written copy. It substitutes a shape for an argument.
Same device wearing a different coat.
Tacked onto a sentence that had already finished.
House style. Prefer parentheses, commas, or hyphens.

shadcn.why: shadcn is how a Next.js agent's hands already work. A kit that only publishes --brand-* variables gets read, agreed with, and then ignored in favour of bg-slate-900. Mapping canon onto shadcn's own slot names is what makes the brand the path of least resistance.

radius_pegs.deviation: shadcn derives its radius scale from a single --radius by fixed ratios (sm 0.6x, md 0.8x, lg 1x, xl 1.4x). That derivation cannot land 6/8/12 simultaneously. We therefore override the derived steps explicitly in @theme inline. The pegs are non-negotiable; the ratio is not.

slot_map.note: ACCENT / ACCENT_DEEP / ACCENT_LIGHT are substituted with the sub-brand's identity accent trio. Everything else is inherited verbatim.
slot_map.muted_foreground_correction: gray-600 #6B6B6B measures 3.94:1 on the dark base and FAILS AA for normal text, so it is the LIGHT-surface muted token only. gray-400 #9A9A9A measures 7.46:1 on dark and 2.65:1 on light, so it is the DARK-surface muted token only. The parent kit had these the wrong way round.
slot_map.distribution: Each kit publishes a shadcn registry: one registry:theme carrying these cssVars, one registry:font, and registry:ui items only where the brand genuinely diverges from stock. Consumers add the namespace to components.json and run `npx shadcn add @<brand>/theme`.

verify.note: Every kit ships a VERIFY.md whose numbers are measured, not transcribed. A kit that fails any check is not shippable.

checks.desc: Re-derive every stated contrast ratio from the hex. Any mismatch fails.
Identity accent satisfies every check in color.constrained_rules.identity_accent.
Every fill token declares a measured legal foreground.
Diff the kit's immutable values against canon. Any drift fails.
Generated globals.css carries the exact radius pegs.
Scan all brand copy for voice.banned_rhetoric patterns.
No raw hex and no raw px literals in component source. Tokens only.
No stylesheet requests a weight the shipped face does not contain.
No shipped SVG depends on an installed font. All type outlined.
No path geometry falls outside its own viewBox.
favicon.ico carries every declared resolution as a real entry.
Every font in the brand guide PDF is embedded as Type0.
All text files are UTF-8 without BOM and free of mojibake.
manifest.json sha256 matches every shipped file.

defects_corrected.problem: --accent-color is #2BCC73, used as the light-mode link colour. Measures 1.98:1 on #F8F8F6. --accent-hover #00AB21 measures 2.88:1. Both fail AA badly.
defects_corrected.fix: Added green-accessible #037B40 at 5.05:1. The bright accent is dark-surface only.

defects_corrected.problem: --text-muted is #6B6B6B, which measures 3.94:1 on #000 and fails AA for normal text.
defects_corrected.fix: Dark muted text is gray-400 #9A9A9A at 7.46:1. #6B6B6B is the light-surface muted token.

defects_corrected.problem: No failure or error colour existed anywhere in the parent system. fragcap had to invent one.
defects_corrected.fix: Promoted fragcap's Fault #E9505F (5.78:1 on dark) and Fault Deep #C0293A (5.46:1 on light) into canon.

defects_corrected.problem: White text on the bright accent measures 2.1:1. This is the single most likely mistake an agent makes with this palette.
defects_corrected.fix: Every fill token in this file carries a measured legal_foreground. Verify asserts it.

defects_corrected.problem: They declare `user-invocable: true`. Portable frontmatter is six keys only; anything else hard-fails claude.ai and Skills-API upload validation.
defects_corrected.fix: Canon fixes the six-key frontmatter contract. Existing kits need this field removed.

defects_corrected.problem: #C24000 measures 4.03:1 as text on the dark base and fails AA for normal text.
defects_corrected.fix: Declared fill-only. White text on it measures 5.21:1.

defects_corrected.problem: The kit's only enforcement artifact is built entirely on `no-restricted-syntax` and `no-restricted-imports`. oxlint 1.79.0 implements NEITHER, and implements no no-restricted-* rule at all. Pointed at that config, oxlint aborts with a parse error. The config has never run.
defects_corrected.fix: Adherence rules are emitted as an ESLint flat config (`enforcement/eslint.brand.mjs`) because ESLint is the engine that implements ESTree selectors. Verified against deliberately-bad source: 9 of 9 planted violations caught, 0 false positives on conforming source. CSS side verified with stylelint: 4 of 4 caught, 0 false positives.
defects_corrected.evidence: VERIFIED BY EXECUTION 2026-08-22, oxlint 1.79.0 and eslint flat config.

defects_corrected.problem: Both reject unknown top-level keys and fail to parse. A generated config carrying a _generated_by provenance field will not load.
defects_corrected.fix: Provenance lives in enforcement/README.md and in a comment header in the .mjs config, never as a JSON key.
